color.gamma: Showing colour values in 0-255 gamma space
color.linear: Showing colour values in 0-1 linear space
color.recent_help: Colours you pick in any colour field appear here
help.appearance.assign: Gives the selected bodies, faces or components a colour or a material look, without changing their weight. Use it to tell parts apart or to preview a finish.
help.component.properties: Shows the volume, mass, centre of mass and moments of inertia of a component, using its bodies' materials. Use it to check weight and balance of an assembly.
help.construct.axis.through_cylinder: Creates a construction axis through the centre of a cylinder, cone or torus face, or a circular edge. Use it to turn or pattern features around a round part.
help.construct.point: Creates a construction point with the method your picks call for: at a vertex, at the centre of a circle or sphere, along an edge, where two lines or three planes meet, or where a line crosses a plane. Use it when you know the references and not the method.
help.construct.point.center: Creates a construction point at the centre of a circular edge, sketch circle or arc, sphere or torus. Use it as a reference for holes, axes and joints.
help.explode.create: Creates an exploded view that pushes the parts away from the assembly's centre, or by the moves you set. Use it to show how an assembly goes together, for instructions or presentations.
help.face.delete: Removes the selected faces and lets the neighbouring faces close the gap, or leaves the gap open as a surface. Use it to take off a rounded edge, a hole or a boss that is in the way.
help.font_details: The interface uses egui's built-in fonts (Ubuntu Light and Hack, under the Ubuntu Font Licence and the MIT/Bitstream Vera licence; Noto Emoji and the emoji icon font, under the OFL and MIT). Sketch text uses Liberation Sans (SIL OFL 1.1). The Crafting Apps' optional font pack, craft-fonts (BIZ UDPGothic, Shippori Mincho, BIZ UDMincho, Noto Sans CJK SC, Noto Sans Arabic; SIL OFL 1.1), is not bundled in SolidCraft builds.
help.frame.member: Places a profile, such as a tube or an aluminium extrusion, along the lines of a frame sketch, one member per line. Use it to build frames, racks and welded structures.
help.frame.rotate_member: Turns one frame member about its own line, by an angle or so a side lies parallel to a line you pick. Use it to square a tube up to a neighbour or face a flange the right way.
help.inspect.accessibility: Colours the faces a tool can reach from one direction, and those it cannot. Use it to check a part for machining or moulding from that side.
help.inspect.center_of_mass: Shows the centre of mass of bodies, each on its own and all together, at uniform density. Use it to check balance and where a part will tip.
help.inspect.colored_components: Gives each component its own temporary colour, without changing appearances. Use it to tell the parts of an assembly apart at a glance.
help.inspect.curvature_map: Colours faces by how strongly they curve, red where the radius is small. Use it to find tight spots and to judge how smooth a surface is.
help.inspect.draft: Colours faces by their draft angle to a pull direction, marking those with too little. Use it to check a part before moulding or casting.
help.joint.origin: Places a named joint origin on a part: at the centre of a face or round end, the middle of an edge, a corner or a point. Use it to prepare where joints attach; one picked on a face follows it when the part changes size.
help.material.assign: Sets what the selected bodies are made of, such as steel, aluminium or ABS. Use it so that the mass and weight match the real part.
help.mesh.convert: Rebuilds a mesh body, such as an STL, as an editable solid with flat and cylindrical faces. Use it to modify imported mechanical parts like a modelled body.
help.panel.native_close: Return a native panel section to its remembered dock without cancelling its content.
help.parts.library: Opens the standard parts: screws, bolts, nuts, washers, set screws, dowel pins and bearings in standard sizes. Use it to add a standard part instead of modelling it yourself.
help.plastic.assign_rule: Assigns a plastic rule to bodies, so their plastic features take its draft and clearance as defaults. Use it to set up a moulded part once for all its features.
help.plastic.boss: Adds a screw boss on a face: a post with an optional hole, draft, root fillet and supporting ribs. Use it for screw points in moulded or printed housings.
help.plastic.manage_rules: Creates and edits plastic rules: material, wall thickness, radii, clearance and draft. Use them to keep the features of a moulded part consistent.
help.plastic.rest: Adds a rest on a face: a round or rectangular pad, solid or hollow, with draft. Use it as a support or standoff in a moulded housing.
help.sheet.convert: Turns surfaces into the rule's sheet metal: the faces of a solid or a surface body, with bends at the edges you pick. Use it to make a sheet metal part from a modelled shape.
help.sketch.arc.center_point: Draws a circular arc around a centre point, from a start point to an end point. Use it when the arc's centre is known, such as a radius around a hole or a pivot.
help.sketch.arc.three_point: Draws an arc from a start point to an end point through a third point. Use it when the arc has to pass through given points rather than around a known centre.
help.sketch.circle.center: Draws a circle from its centre and its diameter. Use it for holes, bosses and other round features whose centre is known.
help.sketch.circle.two_point: Draws a circle from the two ends of its diameter. Use it when the circle's edge points are known rather than its centre.
help.sketch.constraint.concentric: Gives two circles or arcs the same centre, or centres a circle or arc on a sketch point, including the origin. Pick either pair in either order.
help.sketch.constraint.midpoint: Puts a point on the middle of a line, or makes the midpoints of two lines meet. Use it to centre geometry on an edge.
help.sketch.ellipse: Draws an ellipse from its centre, the end of its major axis and a point on its minor side. Use it for oval openings, cams and other elongated round shapes.
help.sketch.insert_airfoil: Reads an aerofoil coordinate file (.dat, Selig or Lednicer) into a sketch as one curve through every point, at the chord you set. Use it to draw wing sections that a loft turns into a wing.
help.sketch.line.midpoint: Draws a line from its midpoint out to one end, with the other end mirrored. Use it for lines centred on a point, such as a symmetric edge.
help.sketch.pattern.circular: Copies sketch geometry around a centre point, over a full circle or a set angle. Use it for bolt circles, spokes and teeth.
help.sketch.point: Places a sketch point. Use it as a reference for dimensions, constraints, hole centres or later features.
help.sketch.polygon.circumscribed: Draws a regular polygon around a circle, sized from its centre to the middle of a side. Use it when the width across flats is known, as for a hex nut.
help.sketch.polygon.inscribed: Draws a regular polygon inside a circle, sized from its centre to a corner. Use it when the size across corners is known.
help.sketch.rectangle.center: Draws a rectangle from its centre and one corner. Use it for outlines centred on a point, such as the origin.
help.sketch.slot.arc_center: Draws a curved slot of a given width along an arc set by its centre, start and end. Use it for adjustment slots around a pivot.
help.sketch.slot.center_point: Draws a straight slot of a given width from its centre to the centre of one end arc. Use it for slots centred on a point.
help.sketch.slot.center_to_center: Draws a straight slot of a given width between the centres of its two end arcs. Use it for slots dimensioned centre to centre, such as adjustment slots for screws.
help.sketch.transform: Scales, turns and moves sketch geometry about a centre point in one step. Use it to reposition and resize a selection at once.
help.solid.box: Creates a box from a length, width and height, from a corner point or centred on a point. Use it for a quick block, a placeholder or a body to cut features into.
help.solid.draft: Tilts the selected faces by the angle you set, measured from a neutral plane. Use it on moulded or cast parts so that they slide out of the mould.
help.solid.revolve: Spins a sketch profile around an axis to make a round solid. Use it for shafts, knobs, bowls and any part that is round about a centre line.
help.solid.rib: Adds a thin wall along an open sketch curve, filled out to the next faces of the body. Use it to stiffen walls and corners, for example in moulded or printed parts.
help.solid.sphere: Creates a sphere from a radius or diameter around a centre point. Use it for balls, knobs and rounded ends.
help.solid.split_body: Cuts a body into separate bodies with a plane, the face of another body or a sketch line. Use it to make parts that are printed, machined or coloured on their own.
help.solid.split_face: Divides the selected faces along a plane, the face of another body or sketch curves, without cutting the body. Use it to give part of a face its own draft, colour or offset.
help.view.grid: Shows or hides the grid in the viewport. Use it as a size and orientation guide while modelling.
import_report.needs_repair_one: 1 part needs repair before it can be modelled on.
import_report.needs_repair_other: {count} parts need repair before they can be modelled on.
navbar.description.separator: A thin line that groups neighbouring slots.
pattern.alignment_hint: Counts include the original. Centre balances copies; Flip chooses the extra side for even totals.
policy.managed_tip: Your organisation manages some SolidCraft settings on this computer.
policy.updates_off: Your organisation turned off update checks on this computer.
prefs.design_tools.hole_snaps_help: The middle of a face and the centres of its round edges.
prefs.dimension_colour_note: The theme's colours, or a colour of your own for the lines, arrows and values. Selection, hover and conflicts keep their colours.
prefs.max_file_size_flag: This run started with --max-file-size {size}, which applies until SolidCraft closes. These settings apply when it starts without it.
prefs.max_file_size_note: Defaults: 512 MB and 256 MB; at most 16 GB. Opening a file takes several times its size in memory. A design that keeps a large import may need a higher design file limit to save and reopen.
prefs.max_file_size_web: The web app opens STEP and import files up to 512 MB and designs up to 256 MB: a browser tab can't hold larger files. The desktop app can raise these limits.
prefs.network_locations_note: For organisations that keep designs on file servers. Off: only servers you allow.
prefs.plugin_remove_note: Remove the installed package and its approved permissions. This takes effect immediately and is kept when Preferences is cancelled.
prefs.select_hidden_edges_help: Edge picks, including for Fillet and Chamfer, can pick an edge behind a face in any visual style. Off keeps v0.30.1 selection behaviour. Hidden bodies stay unselectable.
prefs.sketch.ellipse_axes_note: The major and minor axes as construction lines, so the half-axes and axes can be dimensioned. Off: the ellipse alone, and D on it gives its minor radius wherever the value is pulled, drawn and labelled R as before.
prefs.sketch.tracking_guides_note: Temporary horizontal and vertical guides from hovered centres and edge midpoints.
prefs.sketch_conflict_colour: Conflicting geometry in the conflict colour
prefs.sketch_conflict_colour_note: While a sketch's constraints conflict, the curves and points a failing constraint holds are drawn in the conflict colour too, not only its glyph or dimension. Off: they keep their usual colours.
prefs.sketch_recent_snap: Auto snap to recent centres and midpoints
prefs.sketch_recent_snap_note: While drawing, snap the cursor where the guides of the two most recent circle centres or straight-edge midpoints cross. Off: those guides stay visual and the cursor does not move.
prefs.sketch_state_icons: Sketch icons in the colour of their state
prefs.sketch_state_icons_note: In History and the browser, a sketch's icon takes the colour of its state (under constrained, fully constrained or conflicting) and its tooltip names the state. Off: every sketch has the same icon.
prefs.sketch_tracking_guides_note: Hover over a circle centre or straight-edge midpoint, then move horizontally or vertically to show a temporary dotted guide.
prefs.theme_follow_error: Not applied: {error}. The last good theme stays on.
prefs.theme_follow_launch: Followed for this run only (--theme-file); reloaded whenever another tool rewrites it.
prefs.theme_follow_note: Reloaded whenever another tool rewrites it. Choosing a theme stops following it.
prefs.theme_option_opacity_help: Adjust floating panel opacity. A readability floor protects text over viewport colours.
prefs.theme_option_tab_colours_help: Use this theme’s panel and viewport colours for each ribbon tab.
prefs.theme_option_tab_fade_ms_help: Fade panel and viewport colours when switching tabs. Zero switches instantly.
refused.face_curved: One of its curved faces can't be used for modelling.
refused.face_flat: One of its flat faces can't be used for modelling.
refused.face_freeform: One of its freeform faces can't be used for modelling.
refused.face_rounded: One of its rounded faces can't be used for modelling.
refused.faces_apart: Its faces don't meet closely enough to be used for modelling.
render.aging_airborne_help: Airborne dust is a separate finite homogeneous scattering volume. It changes transport and raw EXR, not the surface-aging stack. Existing volume/glass/denoising restrictions remain explicit; no atmosphere is added automatically.
render.aging_empty: No aging layers: the original surfaces remain unchanged.
render.aging_help: Combine up to eight optical layers, in order. Rust and patina are authored appearances, not age/corrosion simulations. Scale is in world millimetres. No geometry, mass or engineering property is changed; glass and passive stages are excluded.
render.aging_raytrace_help: Ageing is applied by CPU ray tracing and GPU path tracing. Raster keeps schematic rendering.
render.aging_target_help: A named target must still match its captured index and name. Global masks are world-anchored; they do not follow moving parts. This is neither cavity detection nor true edge wear. Filter the list to reach additional bodies.
render.background_completed_frozen: The displayed result is a frozen completed image. Editing a background does not repaint that result automatically. Use Regrade for camera-only changes, or Render for a new physical stage.
render.background_hdr_separate: The current HDR resources illuminate and reflect on surfaces; they are not automatically displayed as a panorama behind the subject. Changing a gradient does not rotate or recolour the lighting.
render.background_lighting_section: HDR illumination · separate from camera background
render.background_no_alpha_override: A camera background is not added to transparent output silently. Raw-master regrading uses captured coverage and does not reapply denoising; the source EXR remains unchanged.
render.background_not_light: Background colour is presentation, not an additional lighting source.
render.background_stage_occlusion: This shot includes physical stage geometry. A large floor or wall can fill the frame and hide a camera-only background. Clear or resize the stage deliberately, or change its physical reflectance. Regrading cannot remove captured geometry.
render.background_workflow: Choose the background you intend: a camera-only colour/gradient, a physical stage that receives light, or HDR illumination. They are independent. Live Preview is a modelling view; render a new image or regrade a retained master to see camera finishing.
render.bloom_help: Creative output-only glow from positive linear highlights, spread with three normalised box passes. Radius is in output pixels. Added in linear display light before sRGB; not a lens, volumetric effect or convergence improvement. The raw EXR is unchanged.
render.check_media_remaining: Density grids, displacement, full spectral integration and propagated polarisation remain unavailable.
render.cpu_area_editor_help: Full side vectors in millimeters; U cross V points towards the emitting side. This differs from GPU half-edge vectors.
render.cpu_budget_not_guarantee: These are admission ceilings, not a RAM reservation or a speed guarantee. Geometry, film and retained previews share the memory budget; rendering remains cancellable.
render.cpu_light_help: Up to eight directional lights. An empty custom list turns them off; selecting a preset restores its lights. Colours are linear RGB and intensity is relative, not watts.
render.effects_gpu_only: These effects require GPU path tracing. Changing the page never switches the renderer automatically.
render.effects_help: Combine ordered colour looks and image-space lens effects. Rendering and raw-master regrading use the same saved settings. Raw EXR stays unchanged. These are original artistic controls, not calibrated lens or branded-film emulations.
render.environment.radial_only: Centre and radius apply to Radial mode.
render.error_finish_gesture: finish the modelling gesture before previewing
render.error_finish_operation: finish the current modelling operation before entering Render
render.glass_model_help: Glass roughness scatters transmitted rays. Dispersion and film colour use three wavelength bands. Rough sheets require straight transmitted shadows off.
render.hdr_primaries_declared: The source declares its colour primaries.
render.hdr_primaries_undeclared: The source does not declare primaries; review the renderer colour requirements.
render.image_scene_stale: Finish the modelling gesture or refresh the scene before checking or starting an image.
render.lens_effects_help: Flare uses up to four separated bright sources in the actual linear image. Ghosts, halo, streaks, chromatic offsets and radial distortion are artistic image-space approximations. Spatial effects need opaque output; outside samples extend the image edge. Grain is deterministic. No physics, EXR or geometry is altered.
render.library_inspect_only: Select to inspect; nothing is applied automatically. Favourites and recent history belong to this open document session.
render.library_rig_help: Fit once at an explicit centre and physical extent. Complete rigs include passive cards; calibration blockers still refuse. Conservative emitter/card clearance is checked before saving.
render.library_source_preview_help: Authored base-colour source map. This is not a rendered or measured material preview.
render.light_preview_help: Live view is unshadowed; Area lights use a centre-sample approximation. Render uses the complete light model.
render.material_map_required: Choose a colour image or a normal image before using maps.
render.material_maps_help: PNG/JPEG up to 1024×1024; 16 MiB encoded total. U and V are orthogonal world-mm repeat vectors (maximum 128 repeats). Colour is sRGB; normal data uses OpenGL +Y. Files are captured at Check/Start.
render.opaque_preview_help: Opaque PBR and simple colours; blended transparency. Refraction, HDRI and final rendering are not available yet.
render.ribbon_studios_help: Browse implemented studio compositions and review their replacements before applying. Concept-only scenes remain labelled.
render.stage_panels.source_note: Authored base-colour source map. Not a measured material.
render.studio_area_help: Up to four one-sided rectangles. Orthogonal half-edges U and V define size; U × V faces the lit side. Coordinates are world-space millimetres.
render.studio_hdr_help: Radiance .hdr, 2:1 panorama, up to 2048 × 1024. EXR is unavailable. The colour assumption applies only when primaries are unspecified.
render.surface_import.complete: Choose an image and enter its author, source and licence.
settings.snap_points: Snap to centre, middle and end points when picking a point
sketch.hint.arc.center_point: Arc: click centre and start, go round either way and click the end, or type a signed sweep
sketch.hint.circle.center: Circle: click the centre, then a point on the circle
sketch.hint.constraint.midpoint: MidPoint: pick a point and a line, or two lines to centre the second on the first
sketch.hint.rectangle.center: Centre rectangle: click the centre, then a corner
sketch.hint.rectangle.edge_center: Edge centre rectangle: click the middle of an edge, then one end of that edge (sets its direction and length), then the width
ui.3d_mouse_looks_like_cap: The reading stays put while you hold it, the way a Return to Centre device does.
ui.3d_mouse_orbit_tip: Traced: the 3D mouse turns the view around the part of the model in the middle of the view when the turn begins, marked by a faint ball. Classic: around the view's centre
ui.3d_mouse_step_pull: Pull the cap towards you, hold it, then let go.
ui.ai_mode_edits_note: Modelling commands run without asking; saving, opening, exporting and other file or destructive actions still ask.
ui.center_arc_follows_cursor: Centre point arc follows the cursor's direction
ui.center_arc_follows_cursor_tip: A centre point arc runs clockwise or counter-clockwise the way the cursor goes round its centre. Off: always counter-clockwise from the start.
ui.colour_vision_note: Changes the colours that carry a meaning: sketch states, axes, bends, analyses and icons. If you use Windows colour filters, keep this Off.
ui.construction.side_hint: Construction line: click the side the line runs towards; right-click to restart
ui.details_curvature_caption: Faces are coloured by their local radius of curvature.
ui.details_draft_caption: Faces are coloured by their angle to the pull direction.
ui.drawing_detail.pick_view: Click inside a view: the region's centre
ui.drawing_detail.step_centre: Click inside a view at the centre of the region to show.
ui.drawing_export.dxf_note: The sheet shown, its lines in millimetres, a layer for each kind of line. Shaded views and images are left out.
ui.export_keymap_tip: Keys, S box favourites and the toolbar, as a file
ui.material_review.claims: Sources and licences are unverified claims. Missing values remain unknown.
ui.mcp_compact_note: For agents connected through the MCP server (solidcraft-cli mcp): inspect_design summarises sketches and tool results are not pretty-printed, so they use fewer tokens. Applies to agent sessions started after the change; --compact or SOLIDCRAFT_MCP_COMPACT=1 also turn it on.
ui.mesh_import_origin_tip: Centre the mesh on X and Y with its base on Z = 0. When off, the mesh keeps the coordinates stored in the file.
ui.properties.inertia_note: About the centre of mass, in world axes (g·{unit}²)
ui.sheet_page.calibration_note: Hold a ruler to the bar and move the calibration until the bar measures 100 mm: at 100 % the drawing sheet then shows 1 mm as 1 mm. The sheet colour is for the screen only; printed and exported sheets are always white.
ui.zoom_to_cursor_tip: The wheel zooms towards the point under the cursor (off: towards the view's centre)
update.prefs_flatpak: Flatpak updates this copy ({version}): run {command} or use your software centre. SolidCraft doesn't check.
